title: Zanchi: second sense of justify is to make the unjust just
source_text: XII. Zanchius vero in epist. ad Ephes. cap. 2. vers. 4. loco de Justificatione, Thes. 13. postquam observavit verbum justificandi duplicem habere significationem, ac primum verbo condemnandi opponi, & significare aliquem a criminibus de quibus accusatur absolvere, justumque & innocentem in judicio pronunciare, subjungit, Altera verbi significatio est hominem ex injusto justum fieri, sicut etiam sanctificari est ex profano sanctum fieri. Qua ratione dixit Apostolus, 1. Cor. 6. 11. Et haec eratis quidam; sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed justificati estis, in nomine Domini Jesu & per Spiritum Dei nostri.
pass_a_gloss: But Zanchius in the epistle to the Ephesians, chapter 2 verse 4, in the place on Justification, thesis 13, after he has observed that the verb of justifying has a double signification, and first is opposed to the verb of condemning, and signifies to absolve someone from the crimes of which he is accused, and to pronounce him just and innocent in judgment, subjoins: The other signification of the verb is that a man be made just out of unjust, just as also to be sanctified is to be made holy out of profane. In which way the Apostle said, 1 Cor. 6:11. And such were some of you; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.
pass_b_english: Zanchi: justify (1) acquit vs condemn; (2) make the unjust just—parallel to sanctify.

lemmas.gloss: to be made just out of unjust
